title: Spark overview
description: What this box is drawing, and what is limiting it. Provisioned from roles/monitoring/files/dashboards/spark-overview.json. Edit in the UI to experiment, then export the JSON and commit it, or the next converge overwrites the change.

panels.title: Power now
panels.description: The whole box, DC side, from the firmware. Excludes PSU conversion loss so a wall meter reads a little higher. Peaks at 171 W on the reference box. Needs `spbm_enabled: true` and a human at the console to enrol the module's Secure Boot key; see roles/spbm/README.md. Empty on a default box is the expected state, not a fault.

targets.expr: node_hwmon_power_watt{job="node"} * on(chip, sensor) group_left(label) node_hwmon_sensor_label{job="node", label="sys_total"}

panels.title: Budget
panels.description: `pl1` as a percentage of its own cap. This is the limit that actually binds on GB10: saturated, `pl1` pins at 139.7 W against a 140 W cap and nothing moves it. The 240 W in the product spec is the PSU rating and roughly 70 W of it is unreachable. Needs `spbm_enabled: true` and a human at the console to enrol the module's Secure Boot key; see roles/spbm/README.md. Empty on a default box is the expected state, not a fault.

targets.expr: 100 * (node_hwmon_power_watt{job="node"} * on(chip, sensor) group_left(label) node_hwmon_sensor_label{job="node", label="pl1"}) / on(chip, sensor) group_left() node_hwmon_power_cap_watt{job="node"}

panels.title: Power cap
panels.description: **Read this before believing any other power number.** 140 W is the stock module budget. 20 W or 30 W means the EC has dropped into its USB-PD safety mode, which pins the GPU near 500 MHz; nvidia-smi cannot see it and only a cold drain clears it. The channel reads the same way in both cases, so the cap beside it is the only tell. Needs `spbm_enabled: true` and a human at the console to enrol the module's Secure Boot key; see roles/spbm/README.md. Empty on a default box is the expected state, not a fault.

targets.expr: node_hwmon_power_cap_watt{job="node"} * on(chip, sensor) group_left(label) node_hwmon_sensor_label{job="node", label="pl1"}

panels.title: GPU
panels.description: Occupancy, not efficiency: a memory-bound kernel reads 100% while the SMs wait.

panels.title: GPU temp
panels.description: Saturated at the stock cap this box sits at 82 °C with zero thermal slowdown of any kind, so heat is not the limiter here and a fan curve does not buy anything.

panels.title: Load
panels.description: One-minute load average against 20 cores.

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: Since the last boot. A firmware capsule only lands on a reboot performed by hand.

panels.title: Targets up
panels.description: Both host exporters. Anything under 2 means a panel below is stale, not idle.

panels.title: Where the watts go
panels.description: The same watts, nested the way the firmware reports them: the GPU rail sits inside `soc_pkg`, which sits inside `sys_total`, which sits inside what arrives from the PSU. That nesting is the whole reason a GPU rail near 100 W is correct rather than disappointing: `pl1` is shared, so loading the Grace cores takes watts from the GPU instead of adding them. Needs `spbm_enabled: true` and a human at the console to enrol the module's Secure Boot key; see roles/spbm/README.md. Empty on a default box is the expected state, not a fault.

panels.title: Power flow
panels.description: Where the watts end up, at the last scrape. `conversion`, `board` and `uncore` are differences between channels rather than channels of their own: the firmware has no accumulator for them. `cpu_gpu` is deliberately absent, because it is a combined rail that overlaps the ones drawn here and would double-count; it is on the time series below. Needs `spbm_enabled: true` and a human at the console to enrol the module's Secure Boot key; see roles/spbm/README.md. Empty on a default box is the expected state, not a fault.

panels.title: System power: the telemetry channels
panels.description: The firmware's telemetry channels, `cpu_gpu` included: it is CPU and GPU combined, so it overlaps `gpu` and `cpu_p` on purpose, and on this box it is their sum. The four PL averages are the panel beside this one, and the `dla` rail is left out because it reads 0.01 W and would draw a flat line at zero. `nvidia_smi_power_draw_watts` is the GPU rail alone and roughly half of `sys_total`. Needs `spbm_enabled: true` and a human at the console to enrol the module's Secure Boot key; see roles/spbm/README.md. Empty on a default box is the expected state, not a fault.

panels.title: The limit that binds: pl1 and syspl1 against their caps
panels.description: `pl1` is the GB10 module budget and the only limit that binds in practice: it pins at 139.7 W against its 140 W cap under a dense bf16 GEMM. `syspl1` peaks at 153 W against a 231 W cap it never approaches. The ceiling is what the cap could be raised to, which is firmware territory: GB10 answers N/A for every thermal-limit register, so there is no Tjmax to raise it against. Needs `spbm_enabled: true` and a human at the console to enrol the module's Secure Boot key; see roles/spbm/README.md. Empty on a default box is the expected state, not a fault.

targets.expr: node_hwmon_power_watt{job="node"} * on(chip, sensor) group_left(label) node_hwmon_sensor_label{job="node", label=~"pl1|syspl1"}
node_hwmon_power_cap_watt{job="node"} * on(chip, sensor) group_left(label) node_hwmon_sensor_label{job="node", label=~"pl1|syspl1"}
node_hwmon_power_max_watt{job="node"} * on(chip, sensor) group_left(label) node_hwmon_sensor_label{job="node", label=~"pl1|syspl1"}

panels.title: At the cap
panels.description: All four limit channels, each within 2% of its own cap, which is the only honest capping signal on this hardware. NVML's throttle reasons are not: they sit above the EC and read Not Active with `pl1` pinned. A workload below the cap is not a fault either, it is a workload that is not compute-bound. Needs `spbm_enabled: true` and a human at the console to enrol the module's Secure Boot key; see roles/spbm/README.md. Empty on a default box is the expected state, not a fault.

targets.expr: (node_hwmon_power_watt{job="node"} * on(chip, sensor) group_left(label) node_hwmon_sensor_label{job="node", label=~"pl1|pl2|syspl1|syspl2"}) / on(chip, sensor) group_left() node_hwmon_power_cap_watt{job="node"} >= bool 0.98

panels.title: Energy by rail over this range
panels.description: From the firmware's own accumulators, so this is a counter increase rather than an integral. Only four exist: `pkg`, `cpu_e`, `cpu_p` and `gpu`. None of them is `sys_total`, which is why the whole-box figure beside this one is computed differently. Needs `spbm_enabled: true` and a human at the console to enrol the module's Secure Boot key; see roles/spbm/README.md. Empty on a default box is the expected state, not a fault.

panels.title: Whole box, this range
panels.description: The `sys_total` gauge integrated over the selected range, because the firmware has no whole-system accumulator. Summed at a fixed 15 s step rather than averaged over the range: an average multiplied by the whole range counts the minutes the box was off, or before spbm was enabled, at the average of the minutes it was on, and overstates the figure in proportion to the gap. Needs `spbm_enabled: true` and a human at the console to enrol the module's Secure Boot key; see roles/spbm/README.md. Empty on a default box is the expected state, not a fault.

panels.title: GPU rail: nvidia-smi against the firmware
panels.description: The same rail, measured two ways, and they disagree. nvidia-smi read 71.9 W against the firmware's 103.4 W at the same instant, 30 to 44% low, and its `power.limit` is permanently N/A on GB10. Diagnose power from the firmware channels or not at all. The gap is also why the safety mode is so easy to miss: NVML cannot see the EC. The lower line is the one to distrust. Needs `spbm_enabled: true` and a human at the console to enrol the module's Secure Boot key; see roles/spbm/README.md. A single line on a default box is the expected state, not a fault.

targets.expr: node_hwmon_power_watt{job="node"} * on(chip, sensor) group_left(label) node_hwmon_sensor_label{job="node", label="gpu"}

panels.title: GPU clocks
panels.description: 2418 MHz is not throttling: it is Default Applications Clocks, i.e. spec. The 3003 MHz nvidia-smi calls Max Clocks is the top of the clock table and not a sustained frequency, so it is deliberately not drawn here as a target line and the gap to it is not headroom. The memory clock is absent because GB10 answers [N/A] for `clocks.current.memory`. A GPU wedged near 500 MHz is the USB-PD safety mode, and the cap on the strip above is where that shows up.

panels.title: NVML throttle reasons, which are blind to the EC
panels.description: **Not Active here proves nothing.** NVML sits above the EC: measured on this box, every reason read Not Active and the SW Power Capping counter did not advance through 75 s with `pl1` pinned at its cap. Kept because an Active reading is still information and because the absence is worth being able to see. The Power row's `At the cap` panel is the signal to trust.

panels.title: NVML: seconds power capped
panels.description: Cumulative since boot, per NVML. Read it next to the panel on the left: this counter failed to advance while the firmware had `pl1` pinned, so a small number is not evidence of a box that is not capped.

panels.title: GPU utilisation
panels.description: Occupancy over the last scrape, beside the throttle history it belongs to.

panels.title: Unified memory (GPU + CPU)
panels.description: This is the GPU memory panel. GB10 has unified memory: CPU and GPU share one 121 GiB pool and there is no discrete framebuffer, so nvidia-smi reports memory.used and memory.total as [N/A], the exporter drops unavailable fields, and `nvidia_smi_memory_used_bytes` does not exist on this box by design. That absence is correct, not a broken panel, and `node_memory_*` IS the GPU memory signal. Do not 'fix' this by adding a DCGM exporter.

panels.title: GPU temperature
panels.description: The die sensor next to the firmware's own zones, which only exist with spbm on. Saturated at the stock cap this box sits at 82 °C with no thermal slowdown recorded, so the fan-curve advice circulating for this hardware addresses a throttle it does not have.

targets.expr: node_hwmon_temp_celsius{job="node"} * on(chip, sensor) group_left(label) node_hwmon_sensor_label{job="node", label=~"gpu|soc|cpu_p_clu0|cpu_p_clu1"}

panels.title: CPU busy
panels.description: Averaged over all 20 cores, so a saturated big-core cluster reads about half. Loading these cores does not add watts to the box, it moves them: `cpu_p` and `gpu` share `pl1`.

panels.title: Load average
panels.description: Against the core count, drawn as a line so the crossover is visible.

panels.title: Network
panels.description: Per physical interface. Docker's bridges and per-container veths are excluded, because a converged box has one of each per project and container and they buried the real link. The reference box is headless on WiFi with no wired fallback, so this is also the panel that tells you whether the link you would recover it over is alive.

panels.title: Temperatures: every hwmon sensor
panels.description: Every temperature the kernel exposes under hwmon. The firmware zones carry a label and are named by it; the SoC, NVMe and WiFi sensors carry none, so they are matched separately and named by chip and sensor. All eight firmware zones carry a real reading, `dla` included, and `tj_max` is a temperature rather than the limit its name suggests: on this box it tracks the `gpu` zone. spbm's power and energy channels are on the Power row, not here.

panels.title: Filesystem usage
panels.description: Per mounted filesystem. Docker overlays, snap loops and the pseudo-filesystems are excluded at the exporter, which is deliberate: mounting the host root into a containerised node-exporter made the filesystem collector recurse them and hang, and that is why this box had no disk metrics at all until the exporter moved to the host.

panels.title: Root filesystem: free space
panels.description: A trend, so a run filling the disk is visible before it does.

panels.title: Root filesystem (holds the shared artifact directory)
panels.description: `/srv/spark` lives here, so this is the number a job writing artifacts runs out of.

panels.title: Targets up
panels.description: Zero here makes every panel above it stale rather than idle. The exporters are host systemd units, not containers, so a target going down is a unit to look at with `systemctl status`, not a compose stack.

panels.title: Scrape duration
panels.description: The GPU job forks nvidia-smi on every scrape, so it is the slow one by construction. A node job climbing toward the interval means the filesystem collector found something to recurse.
